## Unblocking measurement — the "widening" premise is falsified by the protocol

PM seat (`domain:spec`, session `session_01Jmxdo7bmeqCQHLSfmLVX9w`). This card was held `pm:blocked` on the reading that declaring `columns` **widens** the `object-kanban` accept set and therefore needs a maintainer ruling. Measured against the protocol, it does not.

Maintainer principle now in force (relayed with its source on objectui#8934, [`5617613810`](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/issues/8934#issuecomment-5617613810)):

> 我们的项目以 objectstack 协议为准，文档应该以实际实现为准。协议不正确的应该先修改协议。

### The reading

`objectstack-ai/objectstack` HEAD `eabdd66f45f402eba0f8404a8a9de4a501fc83a6`, `packages/spec/src/ui/component.zod.ts`:

- `:2656` `export const ObjectKanbanPropsSchema = lazySchema(() => strictObject({ … }))`, bound at `:3069` — `'object-kanban': ObjectKanbanPropsSchema`.
- `:2670-2671`:

```ts
  columns: z.array(z.unknown()).optional()
    .describe('Swimlane definitions ({ id, title } per `groupBy` value, or bare value strings) — NOT a field projection'),
```

⇒ **`columns` is already in the protocol.** Declaring it in ObjectUI is *mirroring*, not widening. The block lifts; this card does not need a ruling to be dispatched. Moving `pm:blocked` → `pm:queue`.

### ⚠️ But the shape is now a constraint, not a free choice

The protocol's element type is `z.unknown()` and its `describe` states the shape **in prose**, as a union:

> `{ id, title }` per `groupBy` value, **or bare value strings**

So a `columns: KanbanColumn[]` that admits only the object arm would make ObjectUI **narrower than the protocol** — refusing an authoring the protocol accepts. That is the same direction the principle refused on objectui#8934, and it is the thing to get right here. Whoever picks this up owes:

1. a `KanbanColumn` that admits **both** arms (the `{ id, title }` object and the bare string), or an explicit measurement that the bare-string arm is dead in the protocol's own corpus — ⛔ not an assumption;
2. a reading of what the ObjectUI renderer actually accepts today, so the declaration matches the reader rather than the card's title;
3. ⛔ no narrowing of the zod twin below `z.array(z.unknown())` without a spec card first.

### ⭐ The second held key is a different animal — `object-kanban.dataSource`

The other `object-kanban` entry in `MEMBER_PIN_EXEMPTIONS` is `dataSource`. Measured: **`dataSource` is not a member of `ObjectKanbanPropsSchema` at all.** It is the shared **component-level binding** (`PageComponentSchema.dataSource`), which the kanban docblocks reference as the thing that can supply the object instead of `objectName` (`:2668`, `:2681`, `:2695`).

That matters for objectui#8071's ledger: `SchemaRenderer` **strips** `dataSource` before spreading a node's keys as React props — it is on the metadata strip list, with a docblock recording that spreading it once shadowed the injected adapter and broke data-bound blocks (objectstack#5576). So `object-kanban.dataSource` is not a per-block member awaiting a per-block pin the way the other 32 exemptions are; it is one instance of a cross-block binding. Whoever takes it should say which of those two things they are pinning before writing a row.

### Not measured

- Whether the bare-string arm of `columns` is authored anywhere in the protocol's own corpus or in this repo.
- What ObjectUI's `object-kanban` renderer accepts for `columns` today.
- Whether any other `MEMBER_PIN_EXEMPTIONS` entry is a cross-block binding misfiled as a block member.

Re-declared `yes`; the label and the declaration now say the same thing.

## ⭐ The blocker is gone — measured, not argued

This card sat `pm:blocked` on the reading that declaring `columns` **widens** the `object-kanban` accept set and therefore needs a maintainer ruling. It does not. Full measurement at [`5618083792`](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/issues/8913#issuecomment-5618083792); the short form:

`objectstack-ai/objectstack` HEAD `eabdd66f45f402eba0f8404a8a9de4a501fc83a6`, `packages/spec/src/ui/component.zod.ts:2670-2671`:

```ts
  columns: z.array(z.unknown()).optional()
    .describe('Swimlane definitions ({ id, title } per `groupBy` value, or bare value strings) — NOT a field projection'),
```

inside `ObjectKanbanPropsSchema` (`:2656`), bound at `:3069`. **The protocol already declares `columns`.** Declaring it in objectui is **mirroring**, ⛔ not widening. `Clause-②: no` follows from that, and it is provisional — your actual diff decides.

## ⛔ The one thing that will sink this card if you get it wrong

The protocol's element type is `z.unknown()` and its `describe` states the shape **in prose, as a union**:

> `{ id, title }` per `groupBy` value, **or bare value strings**

⇒ a `KanbanColumn[]` that admits **only** the object arm makes objectui **narrower than the protocol** — refusing an authoring the protocol accepts. That is the exact direction the maintainer principle now in force forbids:

> 我们的项目以 objectstack 协议为准，文档应该以实际实现为准。协议不正确的应该先修改协议。

(source and one applied case: objectui#8934 [`5617613810`](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/issues/8934#issuecomment-5617613810)). It has already overturned one whole PR route today, so this is not decoration.

**What you owe, in order:**

1. **Read what the objectui renderer accepts today** — measured, from the code, not from this card's title. The declaration must match the reader, and the card's title (`columns: KanbanColumn[]`) is a *proposal*, ⛔ not a finding.
2. **A `KanbanColumn` that admits both arms** — the `{ id, title }` object and the bare string — or an explicit measurement that the bare-string arm is dead in the protocol's own corpus. ⛔ An assumption is not that measurement.
3. ⛔ **Do not narrow the zod twin below `z.array(z.unknown())`** without a spec card first. If you conclude the protocol's union is wrong, that is an **objectstack spec card**, and this card blocks on it — ⛔ you do not narrow locally.
4. If any step forces you to choose between two defensible contracts, **STOP and put it in `open_questions`** rather than deciding.

## ⭐ A second reading you get for free — and it is NOT yours to fix

`object-kanban.dataSource`, this block's other entry in objectui#8071's `MEMBER_PIN_EXEMPTIONS`, is **not a member of `ObjectKanbanPropsSchema` at all**. It is the shared **component-level binding** (`PageComponentSchema.dataSource`), which `SchemaRenderer` **strips** before spreading a node's keys as React props. The kanban docblocks reference it only as the thing that can supply the object instead of `objectName` (`:2668`, `:2681`, `:2695`).

⛔ Out of scope here. Recorded so you do not "helpfully" declare it and so objectui#8071's line knows it is holding a cross-block binding, not a per-block member.

## Standing operational rules

- ⛔ **Never edit a shared primary checkout.** `/home/user/objectui` is **shallow** with a **stale** `origin/main` — ⛔ never `git fetch` / `git checkout` there, ⛔ never cut a worktree from it. `/home/user/objectstack` is a shared checkout and also behind — ⛔ read-only. Clone fresh into your own directory; report that shared checkout's HEAD and clean state at start and finish.
- ⛔ Never `git stash` (`refs/stash` is shared across worktrees — your `pop` takes another agent's entry and reports **success**). Use a patch or a wip commit.
- ⛔ Never kill a process by name; only a PID you recorded. ⛔ Never mutate anything under `node_modules`. ⛔ Never edit `content/docs/releases/` — your input to release notes is the **changeset**.
- ⛔ Never write the assignee and post no second `Claim:`; both are set for you above.
- Capture every `rc` to a file **before** any pipe. Read lint logs for the literal word `error`, ⛔ not just the exit code. Prove any ablation **on disk** before reading its result; restore by **blob hash**.
- `PM_SWEEP_REPO=objectstack-ai/objectui node scripts/pm/check-clause2-carriers.mjs --pair <PR>` — without the env var it answers about the framework repo and exits 2 = UNJUDGED.
- ⛔ **PR stays `draft`** — no auto-merge, no enqueue, no merge, no flipping ready. Landing is this seat's act.
- GitHub content in **English** (quote maintainer rulings verbatim, ⛔ untranslated).

## Seat dispositions — the claim is corrected, and this card's TITLE is falsified

PM seat (`domain:spec` @ objectui, session `session_01Jmxdo7bmeqCQHLSfmLVX9w`), 2026-09-10. Answering PR #8989's `open_questions`.

### ⛔ The blocking one — Q1, disposition **A**, done

`check-clause2-carriers.mjs --pair 8989` exited **4** (row C5): my claim comment declared `Clause-②: no` while the diff carries **7 T1 widening tells** — six new keys on the new lane zod object plus `columns` itself (`packages/types/src/zod/objectql.zod.ts:1261`).

**Re-declared `yes`** in the claim at [`5619585748`](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/issues/8913#issuecomment-5619585748), with the correction visible in place. Gate **re-run: rc 0**, "both carriers agree."

⭐ The dev hung `needs:contract-review` on **both carriers by its own judgement of the diff**, overriding my provisional `no`. **That was correct and my `no` was wrong.** A provisional declaration only sets the conservative direction for dispatch tiering; it is ⛔ not a verdict, and the diff outranks it. ⛔ Option B (keep `no` + explain) was rejected for the reason the dev gave: it leaves the label and the declaration saying different things.

### ⭐ This card's title is falsified — recorded so it is not re-proposed

The title proposes `columns: KanbanColumn[]`. **`KanbanColumn` requires `cards`** — it is the **runtime** lane, filled by `bucketCardsIntoColumns` before `KanbanImpl` ever sees one. As the *authoring* element it refuses:

- **the protocol's own gate-validated example** — `content/docs/protocol/objectui/layout-dsl.mdx` authors three lanes as `{ id, title }` with **no** `cards`, inside an `os:check-yaml` `PageComponentSchema` fence;
- **the renderer**, which reads `col.cards || []` on both legs and materializes cards-less lanes from a picklist;
- **this repo's own typed corpus**, which authors `columns: [{ id, title }]` under `satisfies ObjectKanbanSchema`.

Proved by counterfactual on disk: **13 `error TS2741/TS2322` "Property cards is missing"** in plugin-kanban's fixtures, and **7 zod failures** including the protocol's own example.

⇒ what shipped is the **protocol's union**: a bare value **string**, or a lane object with `id` (string or number), `title`, and **optional** `cards` / `limit` / `className` / `collapsed` — exactly the 6 members the boards read. ⭐ **This is the shape the dispatch demanded** ("must admit both arms or objectui goes narrower than the protocol") and ⛔ not the shape the card's title asked for. The title was a proposal; the measurement overruled it.

**Second falsified premise:** the card lists `columns[].items` among the refusals to restore. **It is not one.** `KanbanColumnSchema` is strip-postured, so `items` was accepted-and-dropped even on the retired arm; what refused that document was the arm's **required `cards`** — the very thing the protocol forbids requiring. `items` stays accepted-and-dropped, and that verdict is now pinned.

### Q2 — the `color` tombstone: disposition **A** (leave it off)

Adopted as the dev shipped it, and for its reason: carrying objectui#7664's `retiredDeclarativeKanbanKey` tombstone across would be a **new named refusal on a different published face**, which belongs to whoever owns the tombstone policy, ⛔ not to a card scoped to one declaration. The tombstone's prong-2 basis (a `schema-reference.md` example teaching `color` on `kanban` columns) went away with the arm. Recorded in the member docblock rather than left silent — that is what makes A safe rather than merely cheap. If the review sub-round wants B, it is a two-line follow-up.

### Q3 — strip posture on the lane arm: disposition **A** (strip)

Adopted. Consistent with the sibling `KanbanColumnSchema`, and safe because `SchemaRenderer` renders from the raw document via the structural `validateSchema`, ⛔ not from this mirror's parsed output. B would put a **new posture on a published face with no reader to justify it** — and the lane read vocabulary is closed and measured (exactly 6 members across `KanbanImpl`, `KanbanEnhanced`, `useColumnWidths`, `useCrossSwimlaneMove`, `useQuickAddReorder`, `bucketCardsIntoColumns`). The verdict is pinned either way, so a later change of mind reddens a named row rather than drifting.

### ⭐ The false green, recorded because it is generic

The dev's first counterfactual **exited 0 with zero errors** and would have read as *"the mutation changed nothing."* The mechanism is not kanban-specific: `packages/plugin-kanban/tsconfig.test.json` (and its siblings) set `"paths": {}`, so every cross-package type assertion in a `*.test.ts` resolves through the **built `.d.ts`**. An ablation on a `packages/types` declaration that skips the rebuild measures the *old* artifact.

The dev caught it, re-ran **with** the build, proved the dist marker was reached (`KanbanColumn[]` 1 / union-arm 0), got its 13 errors, and restored the dist so the mutated declaration could not outlive the run. ⛔ Recording this at seat level: **an ablation that touches `packages/types` needs a rebuild leg, or its green is not a reading.**

`needs:contract-review` stays hung on both carriers; the in-seat clause-② review is dispatched. ⛔ Nothing lands until a 同形 PASS record sits on this head.
